meta.note: Design languages the user can pick from the explore bar. Each entry describes the shape of the style (surface, edge, depth, corners, type), not its colors: colors come from the project's own tokens. These are conventions gathered from common usage, not standards. Every draft still has to pass the contrast and state rules; where a style and a rule conflict, the rule wins and the style is adapted.
meta.ids: Keep ids in sync with assets/explore/explore-styles.js, which draws the preview tiles.

styles.name: Glassmorphism
styles.summary: Translucent frosted panels floating over a colorful or photographic background.
styles.surface: Semi-transparent fill (10 to 25% of white on dark or colorful backgrounds, 55 to 75% on light ones) with backdrop-filter: blur(12 to 20px) and a little saturate().
styles.edge: 1px border in white at 20 to 40% opacity; often brighter on the top and left edges.
styles.depth: One soft, wide shadow under the panel. Depth comes from layering, not from heavy shadows.
styles.type: Clean sans; medium or semibold weights so text holds against a busy background.
styles.needs: Something behind the glass to blur: a gradient, soft color blobs or an image. On a flat background the effect disappears.
avoid: Glass on glass on glass
Small or light text straight on the translucent fill
Using it for dense tables or long forms
risks: Text contrast changes with whatever is behind the panel: check it against the lightest and the darkest area it can sit over, or put a more opaque layer behind text
backdrop-filter is costly on large or many elements; give a solid fallback with @supports
Respect prefers-reduced-transparency

styles.name: Neumorphism
styles.summary: Soft shapes pressed out of, or into, a single-color surface.
styles.surface: Same color as the page background; no fill contrast between element and page.
styles.edge: No border. The shape is drawn by two shadows.
styles.depth: Paired shadows: a dark one bottom-right and a light one top-left (for example 6px 6px 12px darker, -6px -6px 12px lighter). Pressed state uses the same pair inset.
styles.corners: 12 to 20px, or full circles for controls.
styles.type: Quiet sans; color carries hierarchy because surfaces do not.
styles.needs: A mid-light or mid-dark background (not pure white or black), otherwise one of the two shadows cannot show.
avoid: Using it for everything on a page
Relying on the shadow alone to show that something is a button
Dense data views
risks: Controls have almost no contrast against the page: non-text UI needs 3:1, so add a visible border, icon or filled accent to interactive elements
States (hover, pressed, disabled) are hard to tell apart; make focus a clear ring

styles.name: Claymorphism
styles.summary: Puffy, rounded, toy-like blocks with inner highlights.
styles.depth: A colored drop shadow below plus two inset shadows: light at the top-left, dark at the bottom-right, which makes the shape look inflated.
styles.type: Rounded, friendly sans; heavy weights for headings.
styles.needs: Generous padding and whitespace; the shapes need room.
avoid: Serious or data-heavy contexts
Small components, where the inset shadows turn to mud
risks: White text on pastel fills usually fails contrast; use dark text
Takes a lot of space per element

styles.name: Neo-brutalism
styles.summary: Thick black outlines, hard offset shadows, flat loud colors.
styles.surface: Flat, fully opaque fills; white or one loud color per block.
styles.edge: 2 to 4px solid black (or the darkest token) border on everything.
styles.depth: Hard shadow with no blur, offset down-right (4px 4px 0). Pressed state moves the element into its shadow.
styles.type: Heavy grotesque or mono headings, large sizes, tight leading.
styles.needs: Confidence: few colors, used at full strength.
avoid: Gradients, blur and soft shadows
Mixing many accent colors
Thin borders that look like a mistake
risks: Loud fills behind text need checking; yellow and lime with white text fail
Can feel aggressive for finance, health or legal products

styles.name: Minimal / flat
styles.summary: Mostly whitespace and type; hairlines where a line is needed, nothing decorative.
styles.surface: The page color, or one step off it. No gradients.
styles.edge: 1px hairline border in a quiet neutral, or no border and spacing instead.
styles.depth: None, or one very light shadow for things that float (menus, dialogs).
styles.type: One sans family, two or three sizes; hierarchy from weight and spacing.
styles.needs: A strict spacing scale; without decoration, misalignment shows.
avoid: Adding icons and color to fill space
Light gray text for secondary content
risks: Muted text and hairline borders drift below contrast limits
Buttons can stop looking like buttons

styles.name: Material
styles.summary: Paper-like surfaces at clear elevation levels, filled primary actions, tonal color.
styles.surface: Opaque surfaces; elevated ones slightly tinted with the primary color.
styles.edge: No border on elevated surfaces; an outline variant for secondary ones.
styles.depth: A small set of elevation levels, each a defined soft shadow; elevation rises on hover or drag.
styles.corners: 8 to 16px for cards, fully rounded for buttons and chips.
styles.type: Sans with a clear scale: display, title, body, label.
styles.needs: Consistent elevation: the same kind of thing always sits at the same level.
avoid: A different shadow on every card
Floating action buttons where a normal button would do
risks: Tonal fills (primary at low strength) under text need checking
Looks generic when nothing is customized

styles.name: Bento grid
styles.summary: Content in rounded tiles of different sizes that lock into one grid.
styles.surface: Each tile one fill, one step off the page color; one or two tiles in an accent.
styles.edge: None or a hairline; the gaps between tiles do the separating.
styles.corners: 16 to 28px, the same on every tile; gap of 12 to 20px.
styles.type: A large number or short headline per tile, small label above or below.
styles.needs: A grid with spans (for example 4 or 6 columns) and one idea per tile. It is a layout as much as a style.
avoid: Tiles of equal size, which is just a card grid
More than one message in a tile
risks: On a phone the grid collapses to one column; decide the order
Large tiles with little content look empty

styles.name: Editorial
styles.summary: Looks like a well-set magazine: serif headlines, rules, generous margins.
styles.surface: Paper-like page (white or warm off-white); content is not boxed.
styles.edge: Thin horizontal rules between sections instead of cards.
styles.type: Serif display for headings, readable serif or sans for body, small caps or tracked uppercase labels; a clear measure of 60 to 75 characters.
styles.needs: Real content with a hierarchy. Uses the project's fonts if it has a serif; otherwise a system serif stack.
avoid: Boxes and shadows around everything
Centered body text
risks: Adding a web font is a dependency decision: ask first
Controls need to stay clearly interactive among all the type

styles.name: Dark neon
styles.summary: Near-black surfaces with glowing accent lines and text.
styles.surface: Very dark neutral (not pure black); cards one step lighter.
styles.edge: 1px border in the accent at low opacity, brighter on hover or focus.
styles.depth: Glow instead of shadow: box-shadow in the accent color with a wide blur and low opacity.
styles.type: Sans or mono; accent color for numbers and key values.
styles.needs: A dark theme. If the project has only a light theme, say that this adds one for the explored part only.
avoid: Glow on everything
More than two neon colors
Saturated colored text for long paragraphs
risks: Saturated blue, purple and red text on dark often fail 4.5:1
Glows are costly when many elements animate

styles.name: Soft pastel
styles.summary: Light tinted surfaces, big radii, gentle colored shadows.
styles.surface: Tints of the accent hues at high lightness; each group of content can have its own tint.
styles.edge: None, or a slightly darker tint of the same hue.
styles.depth: Soft shadow tinted with the surface hue, low opacity.
styles.type: Rounded or humanist sans; dark, slightly tinted text instead of pure black.
styles.needs: Two to four tints that sit well together.
avoid: Pastel text on pastel fills
Using tint alone to carry meaning
risks: Tinted text and icons on tinted surfaces fail contrast quickly
Can read as childish for enterprise products

styles.name: Corporate clean
styles.summary: Calm, dense, predictable: the look of dependable business software.
styles.surface: White cards on a very light gray page; a colored header band or sidebar at most.
styles.edge: 1px neutral border on cards, inputs and tables.
styles.depth: Barely any; a 1 to 2px shadow at most.
styles.type: Neutral sans at compact sizes; tabular numbers in tables.
styles.needs: One primary color used sparingly for actions and the current location.
avoid: Decoration
More than one accent
Oversized type and padding in data views
risks: Easily looks generic; let spacing and alignment carry quality
Compact sizes must keep targets at least 24px
suits: anything where trust matters more than delight

styles.name: Terminal / mono
styles.summary: Monospaced type, boxes drawn with lines, the feel of a console.
styles.surface: One dark or one paper-light background; no fills except inverted blocks for emphasis.
styles.edge: 1px solid or dashed lines; ASCII-like dividers.
styles.type: Monospace everywhere; uppercase labels, prefixes such as > or $ used sparingly.
styles.needs: The project's mono font, or the system mono stack.
avoid: Fake typing animations on real content
Low-contrast green on black
risks: Monospace body text is tiring to read at length
Narrow mobile widths break aligned columns
